Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters 
Most 
What makes Abbey College special is what happens beyond the classroom. Our Offer and 
Opportunity Programme (OOPs) gives every student the chance to discover new interests, 
develop talents, make friends and build skills for life. 
This year, we're expanding our offer to more than 50 clubs, teams and activities. From sport, 
music and performance to technology, creativity and academic enrichment, there is 
something for everyone. 
We expect every student to take part in at least one extra-curricular activity. 
Information on how to sign up through MCAS will be shared in the coming weeks. More clubs 
are still being added as staff finalise plans, including some exciting and unexpected 
opportunities. 
We have an exciting year ahead and look forward to seeing students make the most of 
everything on offer. Thank you, as always, for your continued support. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher

Weekly Family Update - 
25.09.26 
Headteacher’s Update: Keeping You Informed About What Matters Most 
There are probably more exciting ways to appreciate the size of a school than through a 
practice lockdown and fire drill, but our first one of the year certainly provided a reminder. 
Watching more than 1,100 students move calmly onto the field, line up sensibly and wait 
patiently was impressive. It is no small exercise, and our students handled it exceptionally 
well. 
We have also been delighted to receive positive feedback about the start of Year 7. Families 
have told us that their children have settled quickly, are enjoying their lessons, and are 
coming home happy and enthusiastic about school. 
Parents have particularly valued the care, support and guidance provided during the 
transition from primary school, helping both students and families feel confident and 
reassured. Staff have also been praised for building positive relationships and creating 
enjoyable learning experiences that help students feel they matter and belong. 
One parent summed it up perfectly: 
     "The transition has felt successful for both our child and our family." 
Feedback like this reminds us of the difference a supportive and welcoming start can make. 
Thank you to all staff for the part they have played in helping our new Year 7 students settle 
so well into life at Abbey College, and we look forward to welcoming our prospective Year 7s 
next Tuesday. 
There is lots more to enjoy in this week's Bulletin. Thank you for reading, and please 
encourage other parents and carers to sign up, as this remains our main weekly source of 
news and information. 
Andy Christoforou, Headteacher 

 
Please read on for essential updates. 
Vacancies at Abbey College and across the Meridian Trust 
We currently have a number of exciting opportunities available. Please share with family, 
friends and contacts who may be interested. Full details and applications can be found here: 
https://www.abbey.college/vacancies  
Celebration of Spirit - Recognition 
 
Headteacher Commendations w/c 21/09/26 
The following students have been awarded with Headteacher's 
Commendations this week for going above and beyond in an area of 
school life.  They will receive 10 Spirit points and a special postcard home.



  

 
 

Staff member of the week 
Miss Clark: Intuition: For your fantastic start to managing New Horizons. It is not an easy 
task, working with our most vulnerable students, and you have made an amazing first term 
for them. You are welcoming, kind and very clear with the boundaries that they need to 
meet. Thank you. 
Tell us about something brilliant! 
If you would like to nominate someone for an Abbey College Spirit Award for any out of 
school success stories, then please follow this link or email the Office office@abbey.college . 
Strong Partnerships 
Parent's Forum 
Date for your diary! 
The date of the next Parent's Forum meeting is Wednesday 7th 
October 5-6pm. You can either join in person in the Boardroom or online via Teams. 
• Please email ParentsForum@abbey.college any questions.  
• Please find our minutes here: https://www.abbey.college/parents-forum  
• If you would like further information on the Parent's Forum, please email: 
ParentsForum@abbey.college   
Genevieve Wardle - Chair of Parent's Forum 
Uniform Update: Optional Plain Black V-Neck Jumper 
To provide greater flexibility for families whilst maintaining our high uniform standards, 
students may now wear a plain black V-neck jumper under their blazer. 
Please note that: 

• The jumper must be plain black, with no logos, branding, patterns, or 
embellishments. 
• It must be V-necked to allow the school tie and shirt collar to remain visible. 
• Hoodies, sweatshirts, crew-neck jumpers, or knitwear in other colours are not 
permitted. 
• The jumper must be worn underneath the blazer, not as an alternative to it. 
Family Quiz Night! 
The Abbey College Parents' Forum invites families to a fun-filled Family Quiz Night on 
Thursday 12th November in the South Hall. 
Gather a team of up to six people, test your knowledge, and compete for prizes, all while 
supporting a great cause. Every penny raised will go towards exciting new opportunities and 
resources for Abbey College students. 

 
Up-to-date MCAS details 
Please ensure that your contact details are kept up to date on MCAS (MyChildAtSchool). 
Having the correct information helps us contact you quickly if needed and ensures you 
receive important school communications. 
You can update your details yourself at any time through the MCAS app or website. 
Alternatively, if you need assistance, please email office@abbey.college with your updated 
information. 

Diary Dates  
 
Everything You Need to Know About Assessments 
 
Ensuring Pupils Feel Safe and Behave Well 
Safety First 
Vaping, smoking, alcohol and drug misuse 
This week, students were reminded about the risks associated with vaping, smoking, alcohol 
and drug misuse. Discussion focused on peer pressure, addiction, health impacts and making 
informed choices. Students were encouraged to seek support if they are worried about 
themselves or a friend. 
Useful Resources 
• Talk to FRANK: https://www.talktofrank.com 
• ASH: https://ash.org.uk 
• NHS Better Health: https://www.nhs.uk/better-health 
• Alcohol Education Trust: https://alcoholeducationtrust.org 

If you need support or have any concerns about your child's wellbeing or safety, please 
contact welfare@abbey.college. We are here to help. 
Promoting Positive Behaviour Every Day 
Student attendance  
Week 3 – Qualifications & Learning  
Your qualifications are built lesson by lesson.  
Each time you’re absent, you miss learning that links to exams and coursework.  
Strong attendance = stronger results.  
Ms Davis – Attendance Officer 
Student curriculum 
How can I find out what my child is learning in each subject? 
Discover Our Curriculum 
At Abbey College, we want every student to feel challenged, supported and inspired to 
achieve their best. Our broad and balanced curriculum combines excellent teaching, rich 
experiences and strong careers guidance to help young people thrive both in school and 
beyond. 
Our curriculum is designed around three simple aims: helping students understand the 
wider world, providing an ambitious education for all, and ensuring that every learner has 
the opportunity to succeed. Parents can explore what is taught across Key Stages 3, 4 and 5, 
along with information about homework, higher-attaining students and relationships 
education. 
Find out more: View our Curriculum Overview

Click here to access this Communication Flowchart on our website.

https://www.abbey.college/key-policies--reports  
Other news updates can be found here: 
• Our news page: https://www.abbey.college/school-communications  
• Facebook: https://www.facebook.com/pg/RamseyAbbeyCollege/posts/  
• Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/abbeycollege_ramsey/

metadata.contentSnippet: An investigation launched after a teenage boy was found on the tracks at St Neots Railway Station has been closed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Investigation launched after boy found on railway tracks closed
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: An investigation launched after a teenage boy was found on the tracks at a busy railway station has been closed. Police were called to reports of trespassers on the tracks between Peterborough and Stevenage at around 6.30pm on September 8. Officers located the boy at St Neots Railway Station and he was taken to a place of safety, the British Transport Police confirmed. A spokesperson for the force said: "Enquiries have been ongoing by officers to establish the full circumstances of this incident. "Following a review of the evidence available, no further action is being taken and the case has been closed pending new evidence coming to light." The incident caused delays to a number of routes between Peterborough and London, including Hull Trains, LNER, Lumo, Thameslink and Great Northern services. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Amazing photos and video show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: Amazing photos and footage show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire and Fenland in their last public display of the year at IWM Duxford.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Amazing photos and video show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Amazing photos and footage show the Red Arrows soaring over Cambridgeshire in their last public display of the year. The Red Arrows took to the Cambridgeshire skies on Saturday (October 3) as part of their final public appearance of the year at the Flying Finale event at IWM Duxford. The display ended the airshow season and marked Wing Commander Jon Bond’s final performance as Red 1 after three years as team leader. The Red Arrows put on a show-stopping display Their final public appearance of the year was at IWM Duxford in Cambridgeshire The team endured a challenging year, flying seven jets instead of its usual nine because of parts shortages affecting its ageing BAE Systems Hawk T1s. The jets have been in service since 1980 and are due to retire in 2030. The Red Arrows have had a challenging year after going from nine jets to seven This was the last appearance of the year for the Red Arrows The Red Arrows also completed a month-long tour of the United States for its 250th birthday celebrations. They were then stranded in Canada for several weeks after poor weather stopped them returning to the UK. The RAF grounded all Hawk aircraft on September 24 after a training accident in Wales, but has since cleared them to fly. Fans in Cambridgeshire had another chance to see the team in action the day before the Duxford display. People turned out to Duxford to watch the air show On Friday, October 2, the Red Arrows made an 18-minute transit flight from RAF Waddington to RAF Mildenhall, passing over parts of the county. Footage by Daniel Hopper shows the jets soaring over the Fenland. The Red Arrows entered Cambridgeshire airspace around 2pm, north-west of Wisbech, before flying over Chatteris. They then flew over Mepal, Wilburton and Stretham before landing in Suffolk.

metadata.title: Woman set fire to deodorant can in attempted arson attack on neighbour
metadata.contentSnippet: An woman who set fire to a deodorant can and put it through her neighbour's letterbox in an attempted arson attack in Chatteris, Cambridgeshire has been jailed.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Woman set fire to deodorant can in attempted arson attack on neighbour
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A Cambridgeshire woman who set fire to a deodorant can and put it through her neighbour's letterbox in an attempted arson attack has been jailed. Beatrice Elliott, 31, was involved in a dispute with her neighbours in Chatteris in the early hours of 14 April. In response, she approached their front door, lit the can and put it through the letterbox. The fire didn’t spread and was put out by a man in the property. Police attended and Elliott, of Barley Close, Chatteris, was arrested. On Friday (October 2) at Cambridge Crown Court she was jailed for 16 months having admitted attempted arson at a previous hearing. PC Boots said: “Elliott’s behaviour that night was completely reckless. "This incident could have been far worse. Luckily, the fire didn’t spread, and nobody was injured.” Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

metadata.title: Trial of former Cambridgeshire councillor charged with sexual offences to begin
metadata.contentSnippet: The trial of a former Peterborough City Councillor accused of rape and other sexual offences is due to begin today.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Trial of former Cambridgeshire councillor charged with sexual offences to begin
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The trial of a former Cambridgeshire councillor accused of rape and other sexual offences is due to begin today. Rylan Ray, 25, of Westgate, Peterborough, faces charges including rape and offences involving sexual activity with children. The charges arose while he was still a serving Peterborough city councillor. He is due to appear at Ipswich Crown Court today, October 5, with the trial scheduled to run until October 30. Ray, who was elected as a Conservative councillor for the Eye, Thorney and Newborough ward in 2022, was charged in 2025 with one count of rape, one of sexual activity with a child under 16 and two of causing a child under 16 to engage in sexual activity. He was also charged with six counts of causing a child to watch a sexual act, three of sexual assault and four of sexual communication with a child. Additional charges included four counts of causing or inciting a child to engage in sexual activity, three counts of making an indecent image of children, and one count of possessing prohibited images of children. He was also accused of possessing extreme pornographic images. Ray is no longer a serving councillor following elections at Peterborough City Council in May 2026.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire residents asked to shape council spending priorities through survey
metadata.contentSnippet: People are being invited to have their say on future spending priorities in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire residents asked to shape council spending priorities through survey
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: People are being invited to have their say on future spending priorities in Cambridgeshire. Cambridgeshire County Council has launched a public engagement survey to gather feedback on its upcoming business plan and budget for 2027–28, which will also include its medium-term financial strategy through to 2029–30. The survey asks residents to share their views on where the council should prioritise spending and savings in the years ahead. Lucy Nethsingha, leader of Cambridgeshire County Council, said: "Every year, the council has to set our business plan and a balanced budget, which is increasingly challenging as demand for services grows and costs continue to rise. "Despite these challenges, over recent years the council has provided much-needed stability in an increasingly uncertain world, and we remain in a stronger financial position than many councils across the country. "We are not immune to the significant cost and demand pressures faced by local government and must make careful decisions about how we use the finite resources available to us. "It is so important that residents have their say so that we can better understand what matters most to people and the priorities they believe are important for the Council. "Your feedback will help inform our business planning and budget-setting process, as councillors consider how best to plan and fund our services for the years ahead. "We hope as many residents as possible will take part in the survey, making their voices heard and informing future decisions about the council’s services across Cambridgeshire." The majority of day-to-day spending is required to support children's and adult social care, education and SEND, with the remainder used to maintain the highways network and deliver community-based services, including libraries and registration services. The engagement survey will be in two phases, with Phase 1 closing on 15 November 2026. To take part, visit Your Voice on the Cambridgeshire County Council website.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been arrested after a crash which seriously injured a woman and teenage girl near Peterborough. Police were called at 8.22am on Sunday (October 4) to Bullock Road, at its junction with Washingley Road, near Lutton. The collision involved a silver Vauxhall Astra and a silver Renault Scenic, Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed. The driver of the Scenic, a woman in her 50s, and her passenger, a teenage girl, both from Yaxley, were rushed to hospital with serious but not life-threatening injuries. Meanwhile, the driver of the Astra, a 31-year-old man from Lincoln, sustained minor injuries. He was arrested at the scene on suspicion of drug driving and causing serious injury by dangerous driving. He has since been released on bail to return to Thorpe Wood Police Station on December 30. Officers are appealing for information and dashcam footage from anyone who witnessed the collision or saw either vehicle in the moments leading up to it. Those with with information should contact police via the force website, quoting 35/NT/19967/26. Have you got a story you want to share? metadata.title: Former Cambridgeshire County Council Green Group leader resigns from party
metadata.contentSnippet: The former leader of the Green Group on Cambridgeshire County Council has resigned from the Green Party.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Former Cambridgeshire County Council Green Group leader resigns from party
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The former leader of the Green Group on Cambridgeshire County Council has resigned from the Green Party. Cllr Elliot Tong, who is also a Cambridge City councillor, said he no longer feels the party will allow him to stand up for what’s right. He led the group on the county council until May of this year, after first being elected to represent Abbey Ward in 2025. He has also represented Abbey on the city council since 2023 and was previously the Green Group’s deputy leader on the city council. Cllr Tong confirmed he will continue to sit as an independent councillor on both councils. He said he had become increasingly disillusioned with the party, who he said had pushed back against building council housing and his support for Palestine. In a statement released on Friday (October 2), he said: “Today, I’ve resigned from The Green Party, as well as the Green Group on both the city and county council. “I entered politics because I wanted to stand up for what’s right. I no longer feel that the Cambridge and South Cambridgeshire Green Party will allow me to do this. “Locally, my Green colleagues have pushed back against council housing in their own wards. “I have been threatened for standing up for Palestinians and told that doing so is unimportant. “Behind the scenes, I have been mocked for my neurodivergence. My loyalty will always be towards doing what’s right, not what’s convenient. “I am excited to continue standing up for regular people across Cambridge.” The two Green Group leaders on the city council, Cllr Sefira Davison and county council, Cllr Darren Green, issued a joint statement in response to the resignation which they said came as a “disappointment and a shock”. They said: “As we’re currently away at party conference at present, we don’t have all the facts on the ground. “Our feeling at present is that in our time in politics, we have come to know Elliot as a campaigner, a colleague, and a friend. “To hear from Elliot that he no longer felt able to stand as a Green was a disappointment and a shock. “We want to go on record first as saying that any form of harassment or discrimination is not acceptable to us, nor compatible with Green values. It should not be acceptable to anyone. “Elliot has been a steadfast colleague and a tireless councillor. His energy, enthusiasm, and support will be missed, and we hope to continue working together for the good of residents on both councils.

news.title: Ramsey Ward Councillor Arrested Over Alleged False Election Statements
news.summary: Ryan Coogan, a Reform UK councillor representing Ramsey Ward on Huntingdonshire District Council, was arrested on September 24 on suspicion of making false statements in election nomination papers. He has been released on bail and is due to return to Milton Police Station on December 22 as the investigation continues.
news.content: Reform councillor arrested over alleged false statements in election papers A Reform UK council group leader in Cambridgeshire has been arrested on suspicion of making false statements in election nomination papers. Representing the Ramsey Ward, Ryan Coogan was elected to Huntingdonshire District Council in the local elections on May 7. Cambridgeshire Constabulary confirmed a man was arrested on September 24 on suspicion of making false statements in nomination papers. The 42-year-old from Waterbeach has since been released on bail to return to Milton Police Station on December 22. Coogan told The Hunts Post he has "worked and will continue to work with the police as part of the investigation". It comes after the force revealed it had launched an investigation into the alleged false statements shortly after the May election. A spokesperson said the inquiry relates to Coogan and the most recent election, though it has not disclosed the nature of the alleged statements. At the time, a spokesperson for Huntingdonshire District Council said: "We are aware of a police referral in relation to the recent district council elections. "As this matter is a live investigation, it would not be appropriate for the council or the returning officer to comment further at this stage." Coogan previously ran as Reform UK's candidate in the Cambridgeshire and Peterborough mayoral election, coming second last year. He was among the party's first representatives on the district council, winning his seat along with two other Reform candidates to represent the Ramsey ward. According to the Electoral Commission the penalties for a false statement on a nomination paper in England and Wales include an unlimited fine or up to one year in prison. metadata.title: 5 Cambridgeshire criminals who were convicted in September
metadata.contentSnippet: Here are five Cambridgeshire criminals who were convicted and jailed in September, including a a paedophile and a "dangerous" predator.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 5 Cambridgeshire criminals who were convicted in September
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Here are five Cambridgeshire criminals who were convicted in September, including a paedophile and a "dangerous" predator. A Cambridgeshire paedophile who believed he was talking to a 13-year-old girl online has been jailed after being caught by a decoy account. David Clark, 52, from Akeman Street in Cambridge, shared explicit messages and images with an account he believed to belong to a 13-year-old girl. He had contacted the account on Snapchat in September 2025, not realising it was operated by an online child abuse activist group. Clark continued to engage in sexual conversations despite being told multiple times that the girl was only 13. David Clark believed he was talking to a 13-year-old girl (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) A "dangerous" predator who raped a woman in a late-night attack near a Cambridgeshire filling station has been jailed for seven years. Darius Andrulionis, 46, began speaking to the victim near the BP filling station, in Lynn Road, Wisbech, at around 3.45am on April 4. The victim begged him not to rape her, but he placed his hands on her mouth and neck to stop her from screaming, leaving the victim fearing for her life. He pleaded guilty to one count of rape before the case went to trial. Darius Andrulionis raped a woman in a late-night attack (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Daniel Hunt, 29, of Queens Walk, Peterborough, was found in possession of 609g of cannabis, £430 in cash, and four mobile phones containing evidence of drug dealing when officers visited a property in Drivers Avenue, Huntingdon, on June 8. The cannabis was worth £2,600 and had been packaged ready for sale. Hunt admitted being involved in supplying cannabis and cocaine and was jailed for 18 months at Peterborough Crown Court on September 2. Daniel Hunt was found in possession of £2,600 of cannabis (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) A drug-dealing disqualified driver has been jailed after trying to flee from police in a late-night chase. Anton Oakley, 37, was sitting in a black Vauxhall Astra in Dogsthorpe, Peterborough, at around 11pm on June 19. Officers became suspicious after seeing a woman approach and then walk away from the vehicle. When officers turned on their blue lights, Oakley initially stopped but then sped off, driving dangerously before stopping outside Tilton Court and fleeing on foot. He was arrested nearby following a short chase. Anton Oakley tried to flee police (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) A man who stole alcohol from two supermarkets in Peterborough has been jailed for a year. Dean Jackson, 43, targeted Tesco in Staniland Way, Werrington, on July 28 and Sainsbury’s in Oxney Road, Parnwell, on August 15. Jackson, of Lincoln Road, Werrington, was arrested on September 25 and admitted the offences at Huntingdon Magistrates’ Court the following day. The sentence also activated a suspended sentence imposed in November after he was convicted of shoplifting and threatening staff with a knife. Dean Jackson stole alcohol from Peterborough supermarkets (Image: Cambridgeshire Police)

metadata.title: Live facial recognition to identify wanted people rolled out in Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: Live facial recognition technology is being rolled out for use in Cambridge city centre after successful deployment in Peterborough.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Live facial recognition to identify wanted people rolled out in Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Live facial recognition technology is being rolled out for use in another area of Cambridgeshire. Following a series of successful deployments in Peterborough, the equipment, which allows officers to identify wanted people, was rolled out in Cambridge city centre on Friday (October 2). LFR works by comparing faces captured by a live camera feed against a police-generated watchlist. It converts key facial features into a mathematical template to identify potential matches in real time. The watchlist includes people wanted for offences, those with outstanding warrants and high-risk offenders subject to court notification requirements. An officer checks every potential match before deciding whether to act. The technology analyses key facial features ad converts them into mathematical representation Images triggering an alert are deleted immediately or within 24 hours, while the images and biometric data of people who do not trigger one are deleted automatically. Deleted images and data cannot be retrieved. Sergeant Luke Charlton from the Cambridge neighbourhood team said: "Live facial recognition is another valuable tool that helps us protect the public by identifying wanted offenders and those who may pose a risk to our communities. "Following successful deployments in Peterborough, we’re now bringing this technology to Cambridge. "It allows us to locate people who are sought by the courts or wanted in connection with offences, helping us bring them to justice more quickly. "We understand people may have questions about how the technology works, which is why officers will be on hand throughout the deployment to speak with members of the public and provide information. "Transparency is really important to us, and we want people to understand the safeguards that are in place." For more information about live facial recognition in Cambridgeshire, visit the force website.

metadata.title: Five new family hubs open across Cambridgeshire to support parents and children
metadata.contentSnippet: A new network of family hubs has opened to support parents and children in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Five new family hubs open across Cambridgeshire to support parents and children
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A new network of family hubs has opened to support parents and children in Cambridgeshire. Cambridgeshire County Council launched the five Best Start Family Hubs on September 28 in Cambourne, Cambridge, Ely, Huntingdon and Wisbech. The hubs aim to offer joined-up support in one place, covering health, childcare, housing and financial wellbeing. Edna Murphy, chairwoman of Cambridgeshire County Council’s Children and Young People’s Committee, said: "Our new Best Start Family Hubs will make it easier for families to access the support they need. "It shows our commitment to giving children and young people the best support possible. "While parenting can be incredibly rewarding, it can also be challenging at times. "Family Hubs offer free, friendly and accessible support, helping families feel connected, informed and confident." The new hubs replace existing Child and Family Centres in each location, but will continue to provide support for families from pregnancy through to age five. This includes stay and play sessions, health advice, infant feeding support, early learning opportunities and parenting guidance. Over time, the service will expand to support families with children up to age 19, or 25 for those with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND). The scheme is part of a national programme. Existing Child and Family Centres across Cambridgeshire will become Best Start network sites, helping to strengthen the family hub offer while continuing to serve their communities. The hubs are free to use and open to all families. They are designed to reduce inequalities and help every child reach their potential. Edna encouraged families to explore the support available. She said: "Whether you’re looking for advice, activities for your child, or support with everyday family life, our Family Hubs, network sites and online resources are here to help. "I’d encourage families to visit their local hub, where they can expect a warm welcome and a wide range of support."

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Cambridgeshire is packed with pizzerias offering distinctive options beyond the major chains. Here are five of the best places in Cambridgeshire for pizza, according to local diners and reviewers. Established in 1978, The Pizza House is described as one of Peterborough’s most iconic independent pizzerias. It is regularly highlighted among the city’s best Italian restaurants. One reviewer said: "The Pizza House has been serving Peterborough for decades. "You must give this place a go and I’m sure you won’t be disappointed." Antonino’s Pizzeria is widely praised on Tripadvisor, with reviewers describing it as serving some of the best authentic pizzas in the Peterborough area. One visitor said: "The pizzas were piping hot and really authentic. I'd recommend the Calabrese and Napoletana pizzas. "The wood fire oven makes all the difference!" Their menu features a variety of authentic Italian dishes such as risottos and antipasti alongside pizza. Wildwood Ely is generally regarded as one of Ely’s most popular restaurants for pizza, featuring classics like calzones as well as gluten-free options. metadata.title: Cambs women urged to attend breast screenings as 141 cancers detected last year
metadata.contentSnippet: A breast care team is urging women in Peterborough to attend their screening appointments during Breast Cancer Awareness Month.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambs women urged to attend breast screenings as 141 cancers detected last year
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A breast care team is urging women in Cambridgeshire to attend their screening appointments during Breast Cancer Awareness Month. North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust is taking the opportunity to remind women aged 50 to 70 to prioritise their breast screening appointments. The NHS offers free screenings every three years to help detect cancers early and improve survival rates. Kaylie Harvey, breast service manager at the trust, said: "Raising awareness of breast cancer – in women and men – is important, particularly during Breast Cancer Awareness Month. Women are being urged to attend their breast screening appointments (Image: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust) "We would urge anyone who has been invited to attend breast screening to keep their appointment. "As part of their regular breast care routine, we would like to remind women about the importance of checking their breasts on a monthly basis. "Women with any concerns or changes should contact their GP in the first instance and they will refer to your local breast unit if required." Breast cancer is the most common cancer in the UK, with one in seven women affected in their lifetime. Around 55,000 women and 400 men are diagnosed with the disease each year. Last year, the trust invited more than 19,000 women for screening, with 14,100 attending. A total of 141 cancers were detected through the programme. Screening can save approximately one life for every 200 women screened – an estimated 1,300 lives each year across the UK. Breast Cancer Awareness Month takes place throughout October (Image: North West Anglia NHS Foundation Trust) The trust is also raising awareness through information stands at Peterborough City Hospital from October 1 to 29, and at Hinchingbrooke Hospital in Huntingdon from October 5 to 9 and October 26 to 29. Breast screening services are available at hospital sites as well as through mobile units, which regularly visit Stamford and Rutland Hospital and other community locations. Further information about appointments is available at nwangliaft.nhs.uk.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire roadwork overruns fall 42% after £424,000 fines and charges
metadata.contentSnippet: Tougher enforcement has helped slash roadwork overruns by nearly half in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire roadwork overruns fall 42% after £424,000 fines and charges
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Tougher enforcement has helped slash roadwork overruns by nearly half in Cambridgeshire. Cambridgeshire County Council recorded a 42 per cent drop in overrun days during 2025/26, following a clampdown that included issuing more than £424,000 in fines and charges to utility companies and other organisations. Councillor Alex Beckett, chair of the highways and transport committee at Cambridgeshire County Council, said: "We know how frustrating roadworks can be for all of us travelling around Cambridgeshire. "Utility companies have a legal right to work on our roads. "Our role is to make sure works on the highway are properly managed and that unnecessary disruption is kept to a minimum." The total number of days works overran fell from 1,191 in 2024/25 to 692 in 2025/26. This reduction indicates that stricter enforcement and financial penalties are encouraging organisations to complete roadworks on time. The council issued 1,443 fixed penalty notices, totalling £196,286, for offences such as working without a permit or failing to comply with permit conditions. An additional £228,350 was recovered through overrun charges. Cllr Beckett said: "It is particularly encouraging to see the number of days that roadworks overran falling by almost 42% in a single year. "This suggests that our approach to enforcement is helping to improve compliance and reduce disruption." He added that higher penalties introduced in January have created a stronger financial incentive for companies to follow the rules and complete works on schedule. The county council issued 36,685 permits in 2025/26, regulating the timing and management of works across the road network. In Cambridgeshire, 51 utility companies are authorised to carry out work on public roads. The council said it will continue to use its enforcement powers to hold organisations accountable and minimise disruption for residents.

metadata.title: Cambridgeshire firefighter retires after 30 years of service
metadata.contentSnippet: A long-serving firefighter has retired after 30 years of service in Cambridgeshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Cambridgeshire firefighter retires after 30 years of service
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A long-serving firefighter has retired after 30 years of service in Cambridgeshire. Group Commander Tony Burton was celebrated at a gathering held at Huntingdon Fire Station on Monday. Colleagues past and present came together to mark his three-decade career with Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service. Tony said: "I have been fortunate to serve in the fire service for 30 years and I have enjoyed my last day as much as my first. "I would wholeheartedly recommend it as a career. "I don’t have a specific favourite memory but collectively I have 30 years of happy memories and being surrounded by people that have been a part of that. "I have had the privilege of working with some wonderful, incredibly talented people. "The fire service is all about the team, and we are only ever as good as those around us. "I have often needed support and guidance, and people have always been willing to give it." Tony began his career at Cambridge Fire Station and later served at Dogsthorpe in Peterborough before rising through the ranks. He eventually managed Ely and Soham stations before taking charge of the service’s training centre in Huntingdon. Matthew Warren, chief fire officer, said: "Tony will be greatly missed by everyone at Cambridgeshire Fire and Rescue Service. "He is highly regarded by colleagues across the Service and has never had a negative word to say about anyone. "As his career progressed over the years, Tony showed a genuine desire to learn and develop, which he was keen to pass onto colleagues, whether they were in the operational world or in a support role. "Everyone wishes Tony all the best for in his well-earned retirement" Tony also thanked his family for their support. He said: "I want to thank my wife, Hannah, and my children, Billy, Florence and Albert. "The fire service is not always a job you can switch off from, and there were times when, although I was at home, my mind was elsewhere."

metadata.title: Visually impaired magician Jo Bannon brings 'The Dirty Work' to Cambridge Junction
metadata.contentSnippet: Jo Bannon's new performance blends magic and visual impairment at Cambridge Junction.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Visually impaired magician Jo Bannon brings 'The Dirty Work' to Cambridge Junction
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Jo Bannon's new performance blends magic and visual impairment at Cambridge Junction. The show, titled The Dirty Work, will run on Wednesday, October 7, and Thursday, October 8. Bannon, who has a visual impairment, uses traditional magic props like a white rabbit and a wand to create a unique mix of truth and illusion. The performance is designed to give audiences a glimpse into a world that merges the seen and unseen, highlighting the often-invisible work that shapes our daily lives. Bannon's performance is not just about magic tricks. It is also a reflection on visibility, disability, and the unseen tasks everyone performs. The show is part of Blind Magic, a collection of artworks by Bannon that explore the performative aspects of visual impairment. Alongside The Dirty Work, the collection includes a film titled Passing and an installation called Sleight of Hand. The Dirty Work will be performed at the Cambridge Junction.

metadata.title: Steam train with 'remarkable history' coming to Cambridgeshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A legendary steam locomotive with a "remarkable history" is coming to the Nene Valley Railway in Peterborough this winter.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Steam train with 'remarkable history' coming to Cambridgeshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A legendary steam locomotive with a "remarkable history" is coming to Cambridgeshire this winter. The Nene Valley Railway in Peterborough will welcome No. 4079 Pendennis Castle—a celebrated Castle Class engine built in 1924—as part of its 2026 Christmas programme. The historic steam train, visiting with the cooperation of Didcot Railway Centre, will remain at the railway into early 2027 for a series of special events. A spokesperson for the Nene Valley Railway said: "We're incredibly excited to welcome Pendennis Castle to the Nene Valley Railway. The famous steam train will remain at the Nene Valley Railway for December and January (Image: Didcot Railway Centre) "This is a locomotive with a remarkable history, from the famous trials against Flying Scotsman to more than two decades spent in Australia, and it will be a privilege to see it operating here. "Christmas is already one of the most special times of the year at the Nene Valley Railway, and having Pendennis Castle hauling selected Santa Specials will make some of those journeys even more memorable. "We're also delighted that visitors now have several opportunities to experience Pendennis Castle after Christmas. "Whether that's getting behind the controls on one of our Driving Experiences, enjoying an evening Fish and Chip train or simply travelling behind this magnificent locomotive on our Winter Warmer service, we're looking forward to starting 2027 in style." In December, Pendennis Castle will haul selected Santa Specials, giving families festive journeys behind one of Britain’s best-known steam locomotives. The historic locomotive was famously trialled against the Flying Scotsman (Image: Didcot Railway Centre) Built at Swindon Works and completed in February 1924, No. 4079 Pendennis Castle was the seventh of 171 Castle Class locomotives made by the Great Western Railway. It shot to national fame in 1925 after trials against the LNER’s new Pacific engines, including Flying Scotsman, on the East Coast Main Line. The locomotive left Britain for Australia in May 1977, where it hauled excursion trains through the Chichester Ranges. After more than 23 years away, Pendennis Castle returned to Britain in July 2000 and is now part of Didcot Railway Centre’s collection.

metadata.title: Charity knitters bring comfort to people with dementia through colourful twiddlemuffs
metadata.contentSnippet: Charity knitters from Somersham and Hemingford Abbots brightened the day for many with their unique creations.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Charity knitters bring comfort to people with dementia through colourful twiddlemuffs
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Charity knitters from Somersham and Hemingford Abbots brightened the day for many with their unique creations. Memory Lane Singing Café in St Ives welcomed Trisha Wiggins-Browne and Maureen Dudley, who presented a collection of colourful knitted twiddlemuffs. These special items, each unique in colour and texture, were created by Trisha, Maureen, and a group of knitters from Mildenhall, set up by Margaret Clowery, formally of Pidley. Twiddlemuffs, decorated with beads, buttons, ribbons, and cords, offer more than just warmth. They provide sensory, tactile, and visual stimulation, soothing restless hands and reducing agitation, offering comfort to those with dementia and Alzheimer's. The vibrant collection was shared among many attendees, who were invited to choose their favourite from the display. Trisha said: "It was so lovely to see people's faces light up with beaming smiles as they received a twiddlemuff." Memory Lane Singing Café is a music-based therapy group for people with Alzheimer's and dementia, and their carers. The café meets every second Monday of the month from 10am to 12pm at Burleigh Hill Community Centre, St Ives. The sessions involve singing to music from various eras, offering a fun and therapeutic activity for attendees. A separate area is available for those who prefer to chat over a cup of tea instead. The café is part of St Ives' dementia-friendly initiative and serves as a networking hub to discover other activities in the community. The café also welcomes other dementia-friendly groups on the other Mondays of the month, at the same time and place. For more details, people can contact Bo on 07851 931099 or John on 07734 264387. Light refreshments are provided, and while there is no entry fee, donations are appreciated. The organisers invite everyone to join them and their volunteers for a fun-filled session of music and camaraderie. The Memory Lane Singing Café is more than just a therapy session; it is a beacon of community spirit and support, making a tangible difference in the lives of those it serves.

metadata.title: St Neots mayor and deputy mayor tackle inflatable course in charity showdown
metadata.contentSnippet: The Mayor and Deputy Mayor of St Neots went head-to-head in a water challenge for charity.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: St Neots mayor and deputy mayor tackle inflatable course in charity showdown
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The Mayor and Deputy Mayor of St Neots went head-to-head in a water challenge for charity. Cllr Catherine Goodman and Cllr Sam Smith took on the inflatable obstacle course at Ride Leisure in Wyboston Lakes on Sunday in support of the Mayor’s chosen charities: Care Network Cambridgeshire, Caring Together, and Access in St Neots. After a safety briefing, both councillors swam out to the start line and began the course with a burst of enthusiasm. Cllr Smith was the first to fall, slipping off the stepping stones, while Cllr Goodman took her first tumble at the crossover point before also falling at the same obstacle. The Mayor and Deputy Mayor tackled challenges at Wyboston Lakes (Image: St Neots Town Council) Cllr Goodman finished the course first, though Cllr Smith managed to stay drier with only one fall compared to her two. Cllr Smith said: "I saw some kids bouncing around the inflatables on the Saturday, making it look easy. "It was not easy. "The kayaks were much more stable and to my liking." The challenge continued with a kayak race, where Cllr Smith took an early lead and maintained it despite the windy conditions. Cllr Goodman said: "The staff made it look easy to walk on the inflatables, but I think they were lulling us into a false sense of security. "I’ve always been at home one the water, but the inflatables clearly decided that I should also be at home in-the-water. The event raised funds for the Mayor’s chosen charities (Image: St Neots Town Council) "I am also informed that it’s the first time a Lemur has completed the course so at least someone set a new course record." Both councillors declined a water jet pack challenge suggested by staff. Ride Leisure said: "We are proud to have been able to assist both the Mayor, Deputy and the charities in their challenge. "Both acquitted themselves well in different disciplines." Donations can still be made at www.justgiving.com/crowdfunding/stneots-mayor.

The incident happened on the westbound A14 between Ermine Street and Brampton Interchange, where a lorry carrying chemicals began leaking and forced the closure of the carriageway. A spokesperson for Cambridgeshire Fire & Rescue Service said at the time: "Everyone is working hard to get the road reopen again as soon as possible but the lane closures are required to ensure everyone’s safety. "We’d advise motorists to avoid the area if possible as delays will continue, possibly for several hours still." A specialist clean-up team was brought in to deal with the spillage. As of 4.45pm on the day of the incident, two lanes remained closed while crews worked to manage the hazard. By 6pm, fire crews had left the scene and the Highways Agency and a specialist cleaning team were managing the incident.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Huntingdon is celebrating the dedication of its volunteers, community groups and partners following this year's Anglia in Bloom Awards. The annual competition recognises achievements in horticulture, environmental responsibility and community participation, with judges visiting the town in July to assess projects and initiatives delivered throughout the year. This year's campaign highlighted the incredible contribution made by volunteers, local organisations and partner groups across Huntingdon. Projects featured during the judging visit included Coneygear Community Garden, Huntingdon Community Centre, Wild about Huntingdon, biodiversity improvements at Coneygear Park and two 3D displays celebrating Sir David Attenborough's 100th birthday and 100 years of Winnie-the-Pooh. Huntingdon received the following awards: · Best large town – Silver Gilt · Best park – Bronze (for Bloomfield Park) · Best churchyard – Bronze (for St John’s Churchyard) · Best crematorium – Bronze (for Huntingdon Crematorium) · Best cemetery or burial ground – Award of Merit (for Priory Road Cemetery) Huntingdon Community Centre won the 'special award for best sheltered housing, care home or inclusivity garden, recognising the outstanding work undertaken by adults with additional needs in maintaining the centre's gardens and growing produce for the Blossom and Bloom Café. The community spirit at the heart of Huntingdon in Bloom was also celebrated at a recent meeting of Huntingdon Town Council, where the winners of the 2026 Best Kept Front Garden Competition were recognised. Christine Scrivener was awarded first place, Sumitha Abayaratne second place and Peter Johnson third place. Stan Mitchell and Debbie Hurley received Certificates of Achievement from the Huntingdon in Bloom Committee in recognition of their participation. Presenting the awards, the Mayor of Huntingdon congratulated all entrants and thanked them for helping to make Huntingdon a greener, more colourful and welcoming place. The Mayor of Huntingdon, Cllr Patrick Kadewere, said: "I would like to thank all our volunteers, community groups, local businesses and the HTC Grounds Team, whose hard work and commitment make Huntingdon in Bloom possible. "Given this summer's prolonged heatwave, their efforts to keep the town looking its best have been particularly impressive."

metadata.title: Hunts families urged to check benefits and bills as living costs rise
metadata.contentSnippet: Nick Blencowe, chief officer at Citizens Advice Rural Cambs, writes his latest column.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts families urged to check benefits and bills as living costs rise
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: As we head into autumn, many households are once again feeling the pressure from rising living costs, higher energy bills and stretched budgets. For some, it can feel like no matter how carefully they manage their money, it simply doesn't go as far as it used to. While we can't always increase our income overnight, there are often steps people can take to make their money stretch further. We regularly see clients who are missing out on financial support, paying more than they need to for essential services, or simply aren't aware of the help available. Even a small increase in income or reduction in household bills can make a real difference over the course of a year. Could you be missing out on benefits? One of the most effective ways to improve your financial situation is to check whether you're receiving all the benefits and support you're entitled to. Many people assume they won't qualify because they work, own their home or have some savings. In reality, entitlement isn't always straightforward and it's often worth checking, especially if your circumstances have changed. A benefits check could identify support such as: • Universal Credit • Pension Credit • Personal Independence Payment (PIP) • Attendance Allowance • Carer's Allowance • Council Tax Reduction We regularly speak to people who are surprised to discover they qualify for support they never thought they could claim. It's also worth remembering that some benefits can act as a gateway to additional help, including Free School Meals, Healthy Start Vouchers, help with NHS prescriptions and hospital travel costs. Free School Meals Since September 2026, all children in England living in households that receive Universal Credit can qualify for Free School Meals, regardless of household income. The support isn't yet applied automatically, so families should check with their local authority and make sure they've submitted an application. Look at ways to reduce essential costs Making your money go further isn't just about increasing income. Reducing regular household costs can be just as effective. It's worth checking: • Whether you're eligible for social tariffs on broadband, phone or water bills. • If you're on the most suitable energy tariff. • Whether you're eligible for any council tax discounts or reductions. • Insurance policies that may automatically renew at higher prices. • Local discount schemes and community support available in your area. Many households can save money simply by reviewing bills they haven't looked at for some time. Keep track of where your money goes It's often the smaller, everyday expenses that add up without us noticing. Taking some time to review bank statements, use a budgeting app or keep a spending diary can help build a clearer picture of where your money is going. Once you know where you're spending, it's easier to identify opportunities to cut back without affecting the things that matter most. Don't wait until a crisis Financial difficulties can affect anyone. Ill-health, redundancy, reduced working hours, relationship breakdown or rising household costs can quickly put pressure on a budget. The earlier people seek advice, the more options are usually available. Too often we see people struggling on alone for months before reaching out for support. There is absolutely no shame in asking for help. Many people are facing similar challenges, and advice services are there to help find practical solutions and make sure people receive the support they're entitled to. Help is available If you're worried about your finances, now is a good time to take stock. A benefits check, a review of household bills or some simple budgeting changes could leave you better off. And for those facing severe financial hardship, additional support may be available through food banks, local welfare schemes, crisis grants and other community organisations. Sometimes a conversation and a quick check can put hundreds, or even thousands, of pounds back into a household budget. That's why it's always worth asking. You can contact Citizens Advice on Freephone 0808 278 7807: 9.30am-3.30pm Monday, Thursday, and Friday, and from 9.30am-7pm Tuesday and Wednesday, or head to our website https://www.citizensadviceruralcambs.org.uk/ for more information.

metadata.title: Village pub wins approval to keep static caravan, guest horsebox and pool
metadata.contentSnippet: A village pub near Ramsey has won retrospective permission to keep a static caravan, converted horsebox and swimming pool.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Village pub wins approval to keep static caravan, guest horsebox and pool
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Find, save and share Public Notices that affect you in the  area. The Public Notice Portal carries statutory public notices published in local newspapers and is the fastest and most effective way of finding out what is happening in YOUR neighbourhood. A village pub near Ramsey has won retrospective permission to keep a static caravan, converted horsebox and swimming pool. The application relates to The Dog and Castle in Woodwalton and sought permission for a static caravan used as living accommodation, a converted horsebox used for guest accommodation, and a swimming pool with a raised deck area. The facilities have already been installed at the site. Council planners concluded the development would help support the continued operation of the village pub and restaurant and would not cause unacceptable harm to the character of the area, neighbouring residents or highway safety. The swimming pool can stay say planners, but there are time conditions on its use. (Image: HDC) Documents submitted for applicant John McGinn said the pub was an important community facility and the extra accommodation and leisure facilities would boost its income. The planning statement said the site already had guest accommodation approved in 2002. The application also explained that the static caravan is occupied by the pub landlord because a recent accident has left them unable to access the first-floor flat above the pub due to mobility difficulties. The Dog and Castle have received retrospective planning permission which means its swimming pool, a static caravan, and a converted horse box can stay. (Image: Google Maps/Street View) The caravan provides level-access accommodation allowing them to continue managing the business. The converted horsebox provides additional overnight accommodation for guests, while the swimming pool and deck area are intended for use by guests staying at the pub's accommodation and by the owner. Residents and a parish councillor raised concerns about parking, traffic and pool noise, but a council planning officer said the proposals would not worsen existing problems significantly. The car park must be properly marked out say planners. (Image: HDC) An officer’s report said residents’ concerns about parking on The Green did not outweigh the pub’s established commercial use or create a serious threat to traffic or highway safety, and Cambridgeshire County Council’s highways department raised no objections. The council also found that the development would not have a significant impact on biodiversity or flood risk. The site lies within Flood Zone 1 and the structures covered by the application are outside areas identified as being at surface water flood risk. Permission was granted on September 30, subject to conditions. These include limiting use of the swimming pool and deck area to between 7am and 10pm Monday to Saturday and between 8am and 10pm on Sundays and bank holidays. The owners must mark out the site’s parking and turning areas within six months and follow the parking measures in their planning documents. Planning officers said the scheme complied with local policy and would not harm residents, parking, highway safety, wildlife or flood protection.

metadata.title: Hunts Philharmonic marks 50 years with six-concert season across Huntingdonshire
metadata.contentSnippet: A music society is marking 50 years of music-making with a season of concerts across Huntingdonshire.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Hunts Philharmonic marks 50 years with six-concert season across Huntingdonshire
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A music society is marking 50 years of music-making with a season of concerts across Huntingdonshire. Huntingdonshire Philharmonic, known locally as Hunts Phil, will perform six concerts in Huntingdon, Godmanchester, and St Ives between October and June 2027. The group was formed in 1977 through the merger of Huntingdon Choral Society and Huntingdon Orchestral Society. Bronwen Rayner, chair of Hunts Phil, said: "Fifty years is a long time for any organisation, but the reason people come hasn't changed at all. "They want to make music with other people on a Tuesday or a Thursday evening. "That was true in 1939 and it's true now." The society now includes around 100 players and singers. Peter Downes, aged 88, joined in 1986 and still rehearses twice a week in the viola section. Mr Downes said: "I have no illusions about being a talented musician, but for two hours on a Tuesday and a Thursday I forget everything else. "I watch the Proms now and think, oh yes, I played that once." Kay Coope, a choir member since the first season in 1977, said: "It doesn't feel like fifty years, but I've definitely become one of the 'nodding grey heads' I used to joke about as a young choir member. "Belonging to a choir gives you a good sing. "It's uplifting, it blows the cobwebs away, and you make new friends." The 50th-anniversary season opens on Saturday, October 17, at St Ives Free Church with a programme of Berlioz, Tchaikovsky, and Dvorak, featuring cellist Joely Koos. Anniversary concerts will also be held on Friday, March 12, and Saturday, June 26, at Hinchingbrooke Performing Arts Centre. Hunts Phil rehearses on Tuesdays and Thursdays in Godmanchester and welcomes new members without audition. Tickets are available at huntsphil.org.uk.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Flag Fen Archaeology Park is gearing up for Halloween with a range of immersive events. The spooky line-up includes ghost hunting, Halloween adventures, and an evening of mediumship. The fun starts with a Paranormal Evening on Saturday, October 3, allowing visitors to explore the ancient site after dark with professional ghost hunters, Spirit Norwich. The evening will feature tales of Flag Fen's prehistoric past from storyteller Michelle Bullivant, followed by a paranormal investigation using various equipment. Paranormal evening (Image: Flag Fen) From October 24 to 31, families can enjoy Halloween Fun, transforming Flag Fen into an autumn adventure for the school half-term. Activities include pumpkin picking, broomstick making, a Fairytale Scarecrow Trail, and a search for missing spell pages in the roundhouse. There will also be opportunities to toast marshmallows around the fire. An Evening of Mediumship with Nicola Ghigi is scheduled for Friday, October 23. The 90-minute event features two sessions, with the Roundhouse Café open for refreshments. Flag Fen's Halloween festivities conclude with Fright Night on Friday, October 30, and Saturday, October 31. The landscape will take on a darker atmosphere, with themed zones inspired by ancient history and East Anglian folklore. Pumpkin patch (Image: Flag Fen) On Saturday, October 24, the park hosts its next Astronomy Evening, inviting visitors to explore the night sky guided by astronomer Dean Watson. With a mix of ancient history, autumn adventures, and spooky encounters, October is set to be a busy month at Flag Fen. For more information, including booking details, visit flagfen.org.uk/events.

metadata.title: We try the Cambridgeshire curry house in the running for a top national award
metadata.contentSnippet: We tried the food at Curry Palace in Cottenham, which is once again in the running for a top national award.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: We try the Cambridgeshire curry house in the running for a top national award
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: Excellent food, excellent service, lovely atmosphere and good value - it is no wonder that the Curry Palace in Cottenham is once again in the running for a top national award. We visited the restaurant on the village's High Street and were impressed from the moment we walked through the door. The clean, modern interior is surprisingly spacious while retaining a cosy feel, giving diners room to eat in comfort. The starter of chicken and king prawns was beautifully presented. (Image: Sarah Cliss) We were welcomed by the restaurant's proud owner, Kosur Miah, who proudly showed off all that the restaurant has already achieved, including the fact that it is a past winner of the 'Champions of Champions' national award in the Asian Restaurant and Takeaway Awards (ARTA). It is currently in the running as an East of England regional finalist in the awards dubbed the 'Oscars of the Curry Industry ', due to be held in London on October 12. Kosur is especially proud because customers nominated the restaurant for another chance to be crowned the nation’s top curry house. The Curry Palace in Cottenham offers diners plenty of space to enjoy their meal. (Image: Sarah Cliss) It is easy to see why customers are taking the time and trouble to nominate as the quality of the food, service and atmosphere is everything you would want from a restaurant. The near-capacity Wednesday-night crowd enjoying the extensive menu was proof of its appeal. Kosur chose our food for the evening, starting with papadams and chutneys. The mango was rich and sweet, the lime tangy and tongue-tingling, while the red sauce was tasty, and the onion salad fresh and crisp. Curry Palace in Cottenham has been named a regional finalist in the ARTA awards 2026. (Image: Google Maps/Street View) Next came a beautifully presented chicken and king prawn starter. The huge prawns were delicately spiced and breadcrumb-coated, while the chicken was melt-in-the-mouth, served with refreshing salad and a tongue-tingling sauce. On to the main, and once again Kosur's choice did not disappoint. Two types of rice - onion and mushroom - both fluffy and light, were served with chicken tawa shashlik karahi - a house speciality - one of the best lamb curries we have ever tried - lamb sagwala. The lamb was tender, beautifully spiced and utterly delicious. The third was a king prawn bhuna, and once again it did not disappoint. The sauce was delicious, and the prawns were perfectly prepared. The accompanying mixed niramish (mixed vegetables) were cooked to perfection, and the garlic naan was sizzling hot and tasty. Unfortunately, the starters and mains were so delicious that there was no room for dessert, but the restaurant offers an extensive choice guaranteed to satisfy all tastes. All in all the experience was a 10/10 - the staff were friendly, efficient and helpful, the food was extraordinarily good, and the ambience was excellent. The Curry Palace thoroughly deserves its nomination, so fingers crossed it repeats its success of 2018 to take the 'Champion of Champions' title on the 12th. Curry Palace was established 26 years ago by Kosur and has built a fantastic reputation for top quality food. More than 1,250 restaurants and takeaways were nominated for this year’s ARTA awards by diners and food enthusiasts.

metadata.title: Man jailed for assaulting baby after Cambs hospital raised alarm
metadata.contentSnippet: A man has been jailed for assaulting a four-week-old baby after doctors at a Addenbrooke's Hospital in Cambridge alerted police.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: Man jailed for assaulting baby after Cambs hospital raised alarm
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: A man has been jailed for assaulting a four-week-old baby after doctors at a Cambridgeshire hospital alerted police. Ernest Oakley, 32, of Swanton Road, Norwich, admitted assault causing actual bodily harm. Oakley took the baby to Norfolk and Norwich University Hospital in November 2023, the court heard, claiming another young child accidentally kicked the baby in the head while the infant was on a sofa. When the baby became unwell, he was transferred to Addenbrooke’s Hospital in Cambridge, where doctors alerted police after questioning Oakley’s account. Oakley was arrested on November 29, 2023, over the baby’s injuries and charged in April 2024. He initially denied involvement but later changed his plea, admitting that, while drunk, he lashed out at someone holding the baby and accidentally hit the child. Oakley was jailed for 14 months at Norwich Crown Court on September 30. Detective Constable Rachel Woods, from Norfolk Police’s Child Abuse Investigation Unit, said: "This was an especially upsetting case, where a tiny baby was injured. "Our team is dedicated to protecting children of all ages and will continue to bring those who seek to harm them before the courts."

metadata.title: 'It absolutely will thrive': First look inside new David Lloyd St Neots
metadata.contentSnippet: The new David Lloyd club will officially launch on October 6, bringing fitness, swimming, racquet sports and spa facilities to St Neots.

summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanTitle: 'It absolutely will thrive': First look inside new David Lloyd St Neots
summary:https://www.huntspost.co.uk/news.cleanSummary: The general manager of a new premium health club in St Neots says he believes the business will "thrive". A new David Lloyd club will officially launch in St Neots on October 6, featuring fitness, swimming, racquet sports and spa facilities. The club's tennis courts (Image: Newsquest) The first 200 members to sign up were invited to preview the facilities on today (October 2). Mayor of Cambridgeshire and Peterborough Paul Bristow and Mayor of St Neots Cllr Catherine Goodman cut the ribbon to officially open the new location. Matt Borer has been appointed club general manager for the St Neots location after 16 years with David Lloyd Clubs. Matt Borer is the club's general manager (Image: Newsquest) Matt said: "I started as a sales manager. "I've been through multiple different clubs, most recently at our head office club in Hatfield and moving over to our Luton club. "I've been on the St Neots journey since April, for the last 6 months." Matt said the outdoor space is one of his favourite features, including the padel courts which he has recently got into using. He said: "For me the spa is absolutely stunning, as well as all the other facilities to be honest, the gym and our clubroom. The club features a spa (Image: Newsquest) "I haven't really got a favourite, I just love the whole club!" Matt said that David Lloyd came to St Neots because the company recognised how up-and-coming the town is. He said: "We're here to embed ourselves in the community and at the club we have our own David Lloyd community. "There's so much here, there's breadth and depth of facilities for everybody and I would definitely say that's the biggest part of us - our community feel. "We've employed over 75 team members, all from St Neots and the surrounding area. "We love it here, all of my team which have moved here from my management we absolutely love it and it's such a beautiful place. "It absolutely will thrive because it's such a fantastic place." The new David Lloyd club will officially open on October 6 (Image: Newsquest) The club will have more than 100 workout stations, heated indoor and outdoor pools, and racquet sports areas. Its courts will include cushioned acrylic tennis courts and padel courts. The new club also features outdoor padel courts (Image: Newsquest) Children will get fun, safe coaching through the Swim Stars and Tennis Stars programmes. metadata.title: Wind farm plans near Mepal advance as environmental consultation gets underway
metadata.contentSnippet: Plans for a major new wind farm near Chatteris have reached another milestone, with the Planning Inspectorate launching a formal consultation on the scope of the environmental information that will be required before an application can be submitted.
